attachments.title: Source clinical note
attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Obstetrics & Gynecology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
1-week history of vaginal itching and increased discharge

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
She describes the discharge as frothy and foul-smelling. She also reports mild dysuria and dyspareunia. Her last menstrual period was two weeks ago.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Tonsillectomy (age 12)

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother: Hypothyroidism
- Father: Hypertension
- Sister: Healthy

SOCIAL HISTORY:
She is sexually active with multiple male partners. She does not use barrier contraception.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On pelvic examination, there is vulvar erythema and a frothy greenish-yellow vaginal discharge. The cervix appears inflamed with punctate hemorrhages. Vaginal pH is 6.0.

LABORATORY DATA:
Microscopy of a saline wet mount reveals motile flagellated organisms. There are numerous neutrophils on the slide.

attachments.title: Source clinical note
attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-07-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Obstetrics & Gynecology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
5 days of frothy, malodorous vaginal discharge and vulvar irritation

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns six months after a previous episode of vaginal itching and discharge. She has been sexually active with one new male partner in the past month and reports consistent condom use. She denies abdominal pain, fever, urinary frequency, or dysuria.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Trichomoniasis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

She is not pregnant and is otherwise healthy.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Tonsillectomy (age 12)

ALLERGIES:
She has no drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother: Hypothyroidism
- Father: Hypertension
- Sister: Healthy

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Social (1-2 drinks per week). Occupation: Graphic designer.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Pelvic examination reveals a green-yellow discharge, vulvar erythema, and punctate cervical hemorrhages.

LABORATORY DATA:
Vaginal pH is 6.0, and a saline wet mount shows motile, flagellated organisms along with an abundance of neutrophils.

PLAN:
Her male partner is asymptomatic and accompanies her to the visit. He expresses concern about possible infection and asks if he needs treatment. The patient is eager to prevent reinfection and would like to complete treatment simultaneously. She is started on the appropriate treatment.
